newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - Infrastructure H-shares seen attractive.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Infrastructure H-shares seen attractive.

text.p: Although the recent financial performance of H-share companies has been far from satisfactory, analysts believe infrastructure firms are a relatively safe option in a record number of H-share issues expected in 1997.
"H-shares have been badly hit by China's austerity policy and are expected to post a big drop on profits in 1996," said Sean He, an analyst at DBS Securities.
"But infrastructure plays such as road- and power-related companies look more attractive," said He.
H-shares are stocks of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
SocGen-Crosby Securities said last month it expects earnings per share at H-share companies to drop by an average 38.2 percent in 1996 compared with a drop of 18.8 percent in 1995.
Despite a more relaxed credit environment in China and expectations of solid economic growth, analysts said they preferred infrastructure companies with guaranteed returns from local governments.
Listed infrastructure H-shares have outperformed the Hang Seng China Enterprise index of H-shares.

Anhui Expressway Co Ltd has gained 29.9 percent since its November debut against a 27.0 percent gain in the index, and Guangshen Railway Co Ltd has risen 25.4 percent since its May debut against the index's 20.9 percent.

The popularity of Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd and New World Infrastructure Ltd, both Hong Kong-based but heavily involved in China projects, has also drawn investor attention to the sector.

China's drive to upgrade its infrastructure would translate into promising growth opportunities in the power sector, said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. "According to Beijing's target for raising installed generation capacity to about 300,000 megawatts by 2000, it needs to increase the nation's capacity by about 20,000 megawatts per year on average from 1996," he said.
Tang said China's austerity plan had delayed some power projects and plans would now have to be accelerated to get back on track.
However, confusion over the country's internal rate of return and the lack of flexibilily on tariff increases has been a cause for concern among investors, one local analyst said.
The disappointing market debuts of Shangdong Huaneng Power Development Co and Huaneng Power International Inc in the United States also remain bad memories for some investors, he said.

Shangdong Huaneng's American Depositary shares were offered at US$14.25 in 1994 and last traded at US$10-7/8 on Friday, while Huaneng Power shares were offered at US$20 in 1994 and closed at US$21-3/8 last Friday.

But Tang said concerns may be eased by the launch of China's state electric power corporation, formed recently to take responsibility for inter-regional electricity supply and unifying the management of the national power network.
With overseas investors offered limited opportunities to participate in China's growing infrastructure sector, analysts said foreigners were keen to buy infrastructure H-shares.
Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Ltd is planning a dual listing in Hong Kong and London in March, market sources said.
The company's listing plans were put back on track recently after a delay late last year due to a weak environment for H-share issues, sources said.

Other Chinese state-owned infrastructure companies on the initial public offering schedule for the first half of the year are Shenzhen Freeway Co Ltd, Jiangsu Ninghu Expressway Co Ltd and Zhejiang Huhangyong Expressway Co Ltd.
